info.name: madlad
info.description:
MADLAD-400 translation service (madlad-api), called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/madlad` → `http://madlad-api:8000`, `include_subpath: true`, methods GET+POST, headers forwarded). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key. Set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth.

Direct access: if you don't want to go through LiteLLM, override the URL of individual requests to `{{madlad}}` — that variable points at madlad-api's host-published port (default localhost:8008 via PORT_MADLAD_API). The direct path is unauthenticated by default; the /v1/madlad LiteLLM path is authenticated by the virtual key. See ai/madlad/MADLAD.md for the operator guide and ai/litellm/LITELLM.md for issuing virtual keys.

Endpoints: GET /languages (list ~400 supported target codes), POST /translate (auto-detect source, translate to target), GET /health (liveness), plus MCP JSON-RPC at /mcp/ exposing the `translate` tool. Note the request body uses `target_lang` — source language is auto-detected, there is no `src` field.

**Error bodies.** Each endpoint's `#### Schemas` section -- at the end of its first request's description, generated from `madlad.schemas.json` by `scripts/api_schemas.py render` -- documents its request body, its success response and every error status whose body is more than FastAPI's `{"detail": "<message>"}`. Any other error answers that `{"detail": "<message>"}`; a request that fails FastAPI's own validation answers 422 `{"detail": [{"type", "loc", "msg", "input", ...}]}`, one entry per problem. A request sent through LiteLLM (`{{litellm}}`) can also be refused by LiteLLM itself before it reaches the service -- 401 / 403 for a missing or unauthorised key -- with LiteLLM's `{"error": {"message", "type", "param", "code"}}`.

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host. Prefix all pass-through requests with {{litellm}}/v1/madlad/… — LiteLLM strips /v1/madlad and forwards the rest to madlad-api on ai_shared.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). The pass-through runs with `auth: true`, so a non-admin virtual key needs `/v1/madlad` in its (or its team's) `metadata.allowed_passthrough_routes` — set under `metadata`, by a proxy admin, because the top-level field is Enterprise-only; the master key works without it. Otherwise 403. See ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Pass-through auth. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth.

Direct-access base URL for madlad-api (bypasses LiteLLM). Host-published port is PORT_MADLAD_API (default 8008); on ai_shared it's http://madlad-api:8000. No auth is enforced at this layer — use only for local debugging inside a trusted network. Swap `{{litellm}}/v1/madlad` for `{{madlad}}` in any request URL to talk to the service directly.
MCP transport session id — paste in the `mcp-session-id` response header value returned by the `MCP — initialize` request. Subsequent MCP calls need it. FastMCP's HTTP-transport session cookie.

item.name: MCP
item.description:
FastMCP JSON-RPC over HTTP forwarded through the LiteLLM pass-through. Note that LiteLLM ALSO advertises madlad-api as an MCP server via `mcp_servers.madlad_translate` in litellm_config.yaml (transport: http, url: http://madlad-api:8000/mcp) — models see the `translate` tool through that path, not this one. The Postman requests below are for debugging the transport directly. Every MCP request MUST use trailing-slash (POST /mcp/), MUST send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, and MUST start with an `initialize` call — copy the `mcp-session-id` response header into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable for subsequent calls.

Unlike a chat completions model, MADLAD is tool-only — it does not appear in `model_list` and cannot be called via /v1/chat/completions directly. Use it by asking a chat model to invoke the `translate` tool, then loop the tool result back (see CLAUDE.md § LiteLLM with Phoenix MCP for the two-step pattern).
